The host has no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or pool job metadata. `review-4172` identifies this review task. The Codex session records the model above.

The complete diff was read against the current laws on upstream main. The old and new cycle inventories follow the research table. The Q208 guard now compares the request with a fixed value. The shared refusal path suppresses the native cycle when it cannot express the request.

### Requested before merge

1. **[P3] NC identity validation: match the complete identifier before selecting a parameter set.** `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:736` accepts a prefix. The branches at lines 741–750 also accept release zero and unsupported variants. With model `iTNC 530`, the real Rust post engine emits G205 without a warning for `340490-03junk`, `340490-030`, `340490-00`, and `340499-03`. The first two strings are read as release 03. This PR newly removes Q208/Q395 for these unknown strings. Bare upstream main keeps its existing parameter list. This bypasses the stated refusal of unknown NC versions. Use one guard for the whole input class. Parse the complete canonical identifier. Permit only the documented service-pack suffix. Check the supported variant and release ranges. Add regression cases for malformed suffixes, zero releases, and unsupported variants. Keep valid identifiers, including `606425-04 SP8`, covered.

### Local validation

### Mutations

The probes used temporary scripts and machine files under `/tmp`. No tracked source changed.

- Q208=500 on `340490-03`: the original guard refuses G205. The mutant compares the request with `RETRACT_FEED_MAX`. It emits G205, so the refusal check turns red.
- Q395=1 on `340490-03`: the original guard refuses G205. The mutant compares the request with `DEPTH_REFERENCE`. It emits G205, so the refusal check turns red.
- An independent JavaScript check also rejects a mutant that forces the old control to the Q208 level.

No run on a physical HEIDENHAIN control was made. Full heavy lanes were not run, per the current review law. The review worktree and branch remain in place to keep the build warm.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Reply to the review of mkinney on head `5c6573102`. Commit `e20797ba4` closes finding 1 (NC identity validation). The new head waits for a fresh review.

**One guard for the input class.** `drillLevel()` no longer matches a prefix. It parses the complete canonical identifier of `dialects.md` section 1:

`^\d{5}\d-\d{2}( SP[1-9]\d{0,2})?$`

The string must have 6 digits, `-`, exactly 2 release digits, and then nothing or ` SP<n>`. The first five digits are the family. The sixth digit is the variant. Then one row of the table `DRILL_ROWS` must match all of these:

- the model;
- the family;
- the variant range: iTNC 530 34049 `0..4`, 60642 `0..5`, 340 422 only; TNC 640/620/320 `0..5`;
- a release that the research names. Release `-00` is never valid.

Each other string with a stated identity gets the refusal by name, as for other unknown versions. A machine with no identity does not change.

**Regression cases.** The new test `a_malformed_or_unsupported_nc_identifier_is_refused_by_name` refuses these strings by name:

- malformed: `340490-03junk`, `340490-030`, `340490-3`, `340490-03 sp8`, `606425-04 SP`, `606425-04 SP0`, `606425-04SP8`;
- zero or unnamed release: `340490-00`, `340490-09`, `606425-05`, TNC 640 `340595-12`, TNC 620 `817600-00`;
- unsupported variant: `340499-03`, `340495-03`, `606426-04`, `340421-02`;
- a valid identifier under the wrong model: TNC 640 `340490-03`.

The valid rows stay covered and now also include `340490-03`, `340494-05`, `606425-04 SP8`, TNC 640 `340595-11` and TNC 620 `817600-18`. The TNC 640/620/320 rows of the earlier tests still pass.

**Gate on `e20797ba4`** (macOS):

- `heidenhain_cycles`: 17 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 220 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The PR body and `docs/decisions/4094-dinsio-cycle-parameter-level.md` give the parse rule and the ranges.

Ready for a re-check.

Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4172 (config `~/.claude-team-skull`), claude-opus-5-5, mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Clean. Re-review of the new head. Safety-tier review (posted G-code). Set `merge-ready`.**

The PR is mergeable. The trial merge with upstream/main `e6849c5ae` has no conflicts. The merge commit's first parent is the PR head `e20797ba4`. Upstream main does not change `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`.

### Earlier findings (review of `5c6573102`)

1. **[P3] NC identity validation: match the complete identifier.** Fixed in `e20797ba4`.
   - `NC_ID` is now `^(\d{5})(\d)-(\d{2})(?: SP[1-9]\d{0,2})?$`. It is anchored at the two ends. The only suffix it permits is ` SP<n>`.
   - `DRILL_ROWS` checks the model, the family, the variant range and a named release. Release `-00` is refused (`rel < 1`).
   - I compared each row with `docs/research/heidenhain/dialects.md` (profiles `itnc-340422`, `itnc-49x`, `itnc-60642x-04`, `tnc320-*`, `tnc620-*`, `tnc640-a..d`). The levels and the release ranges agree. A release that the research does not name is refused. A refusal is the safe failure.
   - The new test `a_malformed_or_unsupported_nc_identifier_is_refused_by_name` covers each case that the earlier review named: `340490-03junk`, `340490-030`, `340490-00`, `340499-03`. It also covers `606425-04 SP8` as valid.

The open change request of the earlier review is met on this head. The `needs-rework` label (set on `5c6573102` to mirror that request) is removed.

### Local validation (macOS, trial merge `60bbcc0c9`)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test heidenhain_cycles`: 17 passed, 0 failed. This includes all six tests in `levels`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 220 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

### Extra suites run

These ran by name inside the quick gate:

- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- `camcraft-app --test conformance`: 7 passed (byte-exact check of each built-in post against its goldens).
- `camcraft-app --test golden_cl`: 34 passed.
- `camcraft-post --test script_heidenhain`: 16 passed. `heidenhain_arc_centre`: 2 passed.

No file under `testdata/` changed. No importer changed. The importer suites do not apply.

### Mutations (in the review worktree only; the file was restored, `git status` clean)

- M1: `NC_ID` back to the prefix form `/^(\d{5})(\d)-(\d{2})/`. Result: red (`a_malformed_or_unsupported_nc_identifier_is_refused_by_name`).
- M2: iTNC 530 `34049` variant range `0..4` changed to `0..9`. Result: red (same test, `340499-03` is accepted).
- M3: remove the `rel < 1` guard. Result: green (it survives). See the optional item below.

### Goldens moved

None. I checked the diff: no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changes. The body says "None". The goldens with `Q395`/`Q208` post on machines with no controller identity, and `conformance` stays byte-exact.

### Optional, non-blocking

- M3 survives because the `rel < 1` guard has an effect only on the `34042` row (`rels: "any"`). The other rows use release lists without 0. A test case `("iTNC 530", "340422-00")` in `a_malformed_or_unsupported_nc_identifier_is_refused_by_name` would pin it. The wrong result is the `q379` level, which is the safe level for this family. Thus this is not a blocker.

### Not exercised

- No run on a physical iTNC 530 340490-03 control. The author's station test (606425-04) shows that the shorter blocks are valid iTNC 530 syntax.
- Full heavy lanes were not run (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review"). This is a P3 PR, so no targeted heavy step is necessary.

The PR author (qsmits) is a collaborator. A collaborator's session can merge this PR through `/merge-ready`.
